conclusions: The exact ArcIn unit-period assumption makes the new data psi_y=psi0_y t^(b(y,y)/2) and tau_yz=tau0_yz t^b(y,z) positive and convergent for the ideal (t), including the two-dimensional coefficient-DVR case. The trace-one coefficient identity gives b(y,w0*y)=b(y,y)/2 and preserves the original primitive line.

The Mumford construction is applied to the actual complete normal pair and original abelian part, coefficient action, line and period lattice. Principal polarization follows with phi=1 and the principal abelian part; no replacement power or field is introduced.

The finite torsion coordinates use the source positive exponent b(y,chi)/k. The exact 2*lcm(M,A) divisibility gives integral exponents. Symmetry preserves the Weil commutator, and compatible roots over each geometric field give the complete coherent Tate marking.

Only ArcIn.eta on bar(Mb)*Lambda is constrained. The final proof constructs the half-label using e_plus in bar(Mb), 1-e_plus in Mb, instead of treating the unconstrained remaining values as additive. The original Tate comparison proves the resulting kernel, independence, additivity and agreement on the selected submodule.

The actual cusp filtration, torus argument and auxiliary Siegel tuple come from the same full marking and original lattice. Every centered-valuation monodromy is v(t)*b, with no independent uniformizer contribution. Lan Theorem 11.4 and its exact Theorem 7.14 cone condition therefore extend the map over the entire base, not merely over its curves.
The unit-period subgroup is X when t is invertible and zero otherwise. Nontrivial X gives exactly the required abelian locus; D(varpi*t) has the original generic moduli object.

All-power ExpBij is used through its actual common-denominator and finite-thickening expansion witnesses. The coefficient convolution is defined in complete finite modules on the proper abelian part. The source character multiplication, cube and compatibility fields prove multiplication, and t_unit/w_rig prove equality of origin evaluation. Hence the generic section-ring isomorphism recovers the same polarized abelian variety and sends zero to zero.

The symmetric cubical line of each competing SAB is relatively ample by Lan Lemma 4.2.1.6. The relative-Proj open immersion detects its formal maps. OLinear, the identified torus and abelian quotient, and Hom(B,T)=0 give coefficient-action compatibility. Normal-base full faithfulness extends the group and line isomorphisms.

PhiRel and the faithful projective theta action recover the selected finite labels; Mb+bar(Mb)=O_E then recovers the complete original half-label. Fine moduli and separatedness give the literal source uniqueness clause.

Nonflat evaluation t->varpi is checked in the actual Mumford affine-chart algebras. Each character coefficient ideal is a principal monomial power, or the corresponding localization; both commute with this specified tensor base change. The original abelian character lines, products and period translations specialize exactly. The represented fpqc quotients and their projective formal algebraizations therefore give the same specialized semiabelian family and primitive line.

Every abstract ring map fixing O-prime and sending t to varpi equals continuous evaluation: its power-series tails map into varpi^r. This proves the full quantified specialization, without any nonexistent map of the full fraction fields.
